title: Duchy of Legnica
capsule: The Duchy of Legnica (Liegnitz) was a Lower Silesian principality of the Polish Piast dynasty, one of many splinter duchies produced by the fragmentation of the Polish realm set in motion by Bolesław III's testament of 1138. During this period Legnica was ruled by Henry V the Fat (d. 1296), who briefly reunited it with the Duchy of Wrocław, and then by his sons Bolesław III, Henry VI and Władysław, who governed jointly before the lands were partitioned again. Through these decades Legnica remained a Piast district duchy nominally within the Polish sphere, predating its later vassalage to the Bohemian Crown, which came only in 1329.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The duchy's boundaries are documented in Bohemian and Habsburg administrative records from the fourteenth century onward; for the period 1248–1329 under Polish suzerainty, boundaries are reconstructed from charter evidence and are somewhat less precise.
